_comment: Conformance ledger — every shared behaviour a driver suite does NOT exercise, and why. A skip that is only prose is indistinguishable from a skip nobody remembers; each entry below is referenced by id from the skip site itself, and tools/test/test-conformance-skips-declared.cjs fails on a skip with no entry, an entry no skip references, or an entry missing a field.

_status_values.platform_gap: The driver does not implement the behaviour at all. Closing the gap means writing the feature, not the test.
_status_values.by_design: The behaviour is deliberately somewhere else — another layer owns it, and replaying it here would test the wrong component.
_status_values.environment: The behaviour is implemented and tested, but this particular host lacks a tool the test needs. Skipped conditionally, not always.

_tracked: Where the work to remove the skip is recorded. "none" means there is nothing to remove — the skip is permanent by design.

entries.subject: _shared/tests/corpus/tap_hold/vectors.json
entries.reason: Linux delegates tap-hold remapping to kanata, so there is no Lua engine to replay the vectors through. The corpus is still loaded and counted, so a malformed file fails here.

entries.subject: _shared/tests/corpus/llm/parser_test_vectors.json
entries.reason: The Linux daemon has no Lua reply parser; the LLM bridge is macOS-only today.

entries.subject: _shared/tests/corpus/prompt_builder/vectors.json
entries.reason: The Linux daemon does not load the shared PromptBuilder, so no code path consumes these vectors.

entries.subject: _shared/tests/corpus/locale/resolution_vectors.json
entries.reason: Linux resolves locales through lib/locale.lua rather than the shared cascade these vectors describe. Replaying the shared backbone here is a roadmap item, not a design decision.

entries.subject: _shared/tests/corpus/tooltip/{layout,dequeue}_vectors.json
entries.reason: Linux has no Lua tooltip layout port; the canonical positioning maths lives in _shared/modules/tooltip/layout.js and the Linux UI does not render tooltips natively.

entries.subject: lib/file_watchers.lua — mtime detection
entries.reason: The watcher tests shell out to stat(1) to observe mtime changes. On a host without stat(1) the behaviour is untestable, not unimplemented — these skip conditionally and run everywhere stat(1) exists, including CI.
